title: Fantasy Player News
description: Breaking Fantasy Football player news along with the impact for fantasy managers

items.author: Ari Koslow
items.title: Brock Bowers (knee) considered day-to-day
items.desc: Raiders head coach Klint Kubiak said Brock Bowers is day-to-day.
items.impact: Bowers did not play in Sunday's season opener after undergoing a meniscus trim. His status remains uncertain for Week 2.

items.author: Ari Koslow
items.title: Zay Flowers (hamstring) considered day-to-day
items.desc: Ravens coach Jesse Minter said WR Zay Flowers is considered day-to-day with a hamstring injury.
items.impact: It is a good sign after Flowers left Sunday's game early after a very strong first half. His status for Week 2 still remains uncertain.

items.author: Ari Koslow
items.title: Frankie Luvu suffers groin injury
items.desc: Frankie Luvu suffered a groin injury in Sunday's loss against the Eagles.
items.impact: The status of Luvu will need to be monitored in practice throughout the week.

items.author: Ari Koslow
items.title: Jordan Magee suffers hamstring injury
items.desc: Jordan Magee is dealing with a hamstring injury from Sunday's loss against the Eagles.
items.impact: Magee pulled his hamstring trying to chase down Jalen Hurts on his long scramble in the fourth quarter. His status will need to be monitored in practice.

items.author: Ari Koslow
items.title: Chris Lindstrom placed in concussion protocol
items.desc: Falcons head coach Kevin Stefanski said RG Chris Lindstrom is in concussion protocol.
items.impact: Lindstrom will have to clear all protocols later in the week to be available for Week 2.

items.author: Ari Koslow
items.title: Tua Tagovailoa (oblique) without update on status
items.desc: Falcons head coach Kevin Stefanski did not have any updates on Monday regarding the team's quarterback situation.
items.impact: Tagovailoa was not available in Sunday's loss against the Steelers. The status of both him and Michael Penix Jr. will need to be monitored in practice throughout the week.

items.author: Ari Koslow
items.title: Michael Penix Jr. (knee) without update on status
items.desc: Falcons head coach Kevin Stefanski did not have any updates on Monday regarding the team's quarterback situation.
items.impact: Penix was not available in Sunday's loss against the Steelers. The status of both him and Tua Tagovailoa will need to be monitored in practice throughout the week.

items.author: Ari Koslow
items.title: Alec Pierce suffers hand/wrist bruise, expected to be fine
items.desc: Colts head coach Shane Steichen said Alec Pierce's left hand/wrist is fine.
items.impact: Pierce said he is dealing with a bruise. His status will need to be monitored in practice this week.

items.author: Ari Koslow
items.title: Jordan Mason being evaluated for sore thumb
items.desc: Vikings head coach Kevin Stefanski said RB Jordan Mason is being evaluated for a sore thumb.
items.impact: Mason came into the building on Monday with the injury. He is day-to-day for now after leading the backfield on Sunday.

items.author: Ari Koslow
items.title: Dylan Sampson (knee) being evaluated
items.desc: Browns head coach Todd Monken said the team is still evaluating the severity of RB Dylan Sampson's knee injury.
items.impact: Sampson did not play in the second half on Sunday. The team is expected to know more on Wednesday.

items.author: Ari Koslow
items.title: Jalen Coker (ankle) in walking boot, not expected to miss time this week
items.desc: Jalen Coker was in a walking boot on Monday, but he is not expected to miss time this week.
items.impact: Coker rolled his left ankle in the first quarter on Sunday. He still went on to have a career day. His status will have to be monitored this week, but he is currently expected to be good to go for Week 2.

items.author: Ari Koslow
items.title: Kyler Murray (concussion) status for Week 2 uncertain
items.desc: The Vikings reportedly do not know if Kyler Murray will progress through concussion protocol in time to play in Week 2's game against the Bears.
items.impact: Murray took an ugly hit in Sunday's game against the Packers. He will have to clear concussion protocol to be able to return for Week 2. Carson Wentz is seemingly likely to see the start for Minnesota as of now.

items.author: Ari Koslow
items.title: Minkah Fitzpatrick (groin) without update on status
items.desc: Jets head coach Aaron Glenn said he does not have an update on Minkah Fitzpatrick's groin injury.
items.impact: Fitzpatrick suffered the injury in Sunday's win over the Titans. His status will need to be monitored in practice this week.

items.author: Ari Koslow
items.title: Myles Garrett (knee) without timetable to return
items.desc: Rams head coach Sean McVay said he doesn't have a timeline for when Myles Garrett will return.
items.impact: Garrett was placed on injured reserve, meaning he will miss at least the next four games. It appears he could miss more time after undergoing surgery.

items.author: Ari Koslow
items.title: Aaron Donald uncertain for Week 2
items.desc: Rams head coach Sean McVay said the team is undecided on whether or not Aaron Donald will play in Week 2 against the Giants.
items.impact: Donald did not play in the season opener against the 49ers last week. The Rams will already be without Myles Garrett after placing him on IR. The status of Donald will need to be monitored ahead of next Monday's game.

items.author: Ari Koslow
items.title: Jacob Parrish dealing with back sprain
items.desc: Buccaneers coach Todd Bowles said CB Jacob Parrish has a back sprain.
items.impact: Parrish underwent X-rays that returned negative. He is week-to-week for now.

items.author: Ari Koslow
items.title: Henry To'oTo'o (shoulder) to miss some time
items.desc: Texans head coach DeMeco Ryans said LB Henry To'oTo'o "will be out for some time" with a shoulder injury.
items.impact: To'oTo'o left early in the second half in Sunday's game against the Bills. He appears to be week-to-week for now.

items.author: Ari Koslow
items.title: Ladd McConkey (rib) undergoing testing
items.desc: Chargers WR Ladd McConkey will undergo testing to determine the severity of his rib injury.
items.impact: There should be an update provided on McConkey later this week. He caught five passes for 82 yards and a touchdown before taking an ugly hit on Sunday. His status is uncertain for Week 2 against the Raiders.

items.author: Ari Koslow
items.title: Deshaun Watson 'anticipated' to start Week 2 for Browns
items.desc: Browns coach Todd Monken said he "anticipates" Deshaun Watson will start for the Browns in Week 2.
items.impact: Not ideal. It was an ugly showing again for the Browns offense led by Watson on Sunday. The entire Browns offense remains downgraded for now for fantasy managers.

items.author: Garrett Ball
items.title: Brian Thomas Jr. (shoulder) will be limited this week, hopeful for Denver
items.desc: Brian Thomas Jr. (shoulder) will be limited in practice this week, per HC Liam Coen. However, Coen noted that the reciever should be good to go against Denver.
items.impact: It's great news for fantasy managers who were hoping to see more from BTJ before he exited early in what ended up being a blowout win. Thomas is looking to bounce back after a down sophomore season, but facing Denver while coming off of injury is a much harder task than facing Cleveland's secondary.

items.author: Garrett Ball
items.title: Malik Hooker (arm) suffers fractured forearm, out several weeks
items.desc: Malik Hooker (arm) suffered a fracture in his forearm on Sunday and will consult specialists as to exactly how long he will be out.
items.impact: Hooker left the Cowboys game against the Giants in the fourth quarter and did not return. With Hooker out, P.J. Locke is likely next in line for snaps.

items.author: Chris Schommer
items.title: Colts D/ST shredded in Week 1 loss
items.desc: The Colts D/ST forced one turnover (one fumble recovery) while also registering two sacks in a 41-23 loss to the Baltimore Ravens in Week 1.
items.impact: The unit had no answers for a dynamic Ravens offense in the season opener, allowing 506 offensive yards highlighted by four rushing touchdowns in the win. The defense will be difficult to trust in Week 2 against a Kansas City Chiefs offense led by quarterback Patrick Mahomes and free-agent acquisition Kenneth Walker III.

items.author: Chris Schommer
items.title: Spencer Shrader misses extra point in Week 1
items.desc: Spencer Shrader converted his only field goal attempt as well as two of his three extra point attempts to finish with five points in the Colts' 41-23 loss to the Baltimore Ravens in Week 1.
items.impact: Shrader fell victim behind an underwhelming performance from the Indianapolis offense in the season opener. The kicker will hope for more opportunities in a difficult Week 2 contest against the Kansas City Chiefs.

items.author: Garrett Ball
items.title: Ben Brown (knee) will return to practice on Monday
items.desc: Ben Brown (knee) will return to Patriots practice on Monday.
items.impact: Brown missed the Patriots' season-opening loss to the Seahawks, but getting back to practice opens up the potential for his return in Week 2.

items.author: Chris Schommer
items.title: Saints D/ST quiet in Week 1
items.desc: The Saints D/ST forced one turnover (one fumble recovery) while also recording one sack in a 31-30 loss to the Detroit Lions in Week 1.
items.impact: The unit struggled to contain dynamic running back Jahmyr Gibbs, allowing 5.4 yards per carry to the electric running back. The defense faces another tough rushing attack from the Baltimore Ravens in Week 2.

items.author: Garrett Ball
items.title: TreVeyon Henderson returning to practice on Monday
items.desc: TreVeyon Henderson (ankle) is returning to practice on Monday.
items.impact: Henderson missed the Patriots game against Seattle on Wednesday, but is hopefully going to make his return to the field for Week 2. Should he play, it will be interesting to see how things are divvied up between him and Rhamondre Stevenson. Stevenson wasn't particularly efficient at first glance, but looking deeper, he had to do a lot of work after contact, so his box score might not be as bad as thought.

items.author: Chris Schommer
items.title: Daniel Carlson misses field goal in Week 1
items.desc: Daniel Carlson converted all three of his extra point attempts as well as one of his two field goal attempts to finish with six points in the Saints' 31-30 loss to the Detroit Lions in Week 1.
items.impact: Carlson was unable to convert on a 60-yard field goal on an otherwise solid season-opening performance. The kicker remains difficult to trust behind an inconsistent New Orleans offense, with a Week 2 contest against the Baltimore Ravens up next.

items.author: Chris Schommer
items.title: Lions D/ST stands tall in Week 1 win
items.desc: The Lions D/ST forced three turnovers (two interceptions, one fumble recovery) while also picking up five sacks in a 31-30 Week 1 win over the New Orleans Saints.
items.impact: The unit escaped after allowing the Saints to come back from a 21-0 deficit in the second half, with New Orleans quarterback Tyler Shough overthrowing a potential game-winning two-point conversion in overtime. Fantasy managers will need to have another option available with a Week 2 matchup against the Buffalo Bills up next.

items.author: Chris Schommer
items.title: Jake Bates picks up seven points in Week 1
items.desc: Jake Bates converted all four of his extra point attempts as well as his lone field goal attempt to finish with seven points in the Lions' 31-30 win over the New Orleans Saints in Week 1.
items.impact: Bates made the most of his opportunities behind a Detroit offense that battled consistency issues in the season opener. The kicker should once again be in line for plenty of opportunities in what should be a high-scoring Week 2 matchup against the Buffalo Bills.

items.author: Chris Schommer
items.title: Bears D/ST torched through air in Week 1
items.desc: The Bears D/ST forced two turnovers (one interception, one fumble recovery) while also registering two sacks in a 59-37 win over the Carolina Panthers in Week 1.
items.impact: The unit struggled to stop the Carolina offense through the air, allowing over 350 passing yards and three passing touchdowns in the win. The unit will look to get back on track in a Week 2 divisional contest against the Minnesota Vikings.

items.author: Chris Schommer
items.title: Cairo Santos perfect in Week 1
items.desc: Cairo Santos converted his only field goal attempt as well as all eight of his extra point attempts to finish with 11 points in the Bears' 59-37 win over the Carolina Panthers in Week 1.
items.impact: Santos benefited from a high-octane Chicago offensive attack, finishing with double-digit points in the win. The veteran kicker should continue to see plenty of opportunities as the season moves forward for fantasy managers, with a Week 2 contest against the Minnesota Vikings up next.

items.author: Chris Schommer
items.title: Panthers D/ST dismal in Week 1 loss
items.desc: The Panthers D/ST forced one turnover (one fumble recovery) while also recording two sacks in a 59-37 Week 1 loss to the Chicago Bears.
items.impact: The unit did not have many answers for an explosive Chicago offense in the season opener, allowing eight total touchdowns on 592 offensive yards, with six of those scores coming on the ground in the loss. The unit will look to get back on track against an Atlanta Falcons offense that could be forced to once again start quarterback Cooper Rush in Week 2.

items.author: Chris Schommer
items.title: Ryan Fitzgerald misses extra point in Week 1
items.desc: Ryan Fitzgerald converted his lone field goal attempt as well as four of his five extra point attempts to finish with seven points in the Panthers' 59-37 loss to the Chicago Bears in Week 1.
items.impact: Fitzgerald turned in a mostly solid performance, with the missed extra point the outlier. The kicker will look for more success in a Week 2 divisional contest against the Atlanta Falcons.

items.author: Chris Schommer
items.title: Dolphins D/ST records two interceptions in Week 1
items.desc: The Dolphins D/ST recorded two interceptions while failing to pick up any sacks in a 27-13 loss to the Las Vegas Raiders in Week 1.
items.impact: The unit mostly did its part in a losing effort, allowing less than 300 offensive yards on the day. Fantasy managers cannot trust the defense against a tough San Francisco 49ers offense in Week 2.

items.author: Garrett Ball
items.title: Dean Clark expected to sign with Jets practice squad
items.desc: Dean Clark is expected to re-sign with the Jets practice squad. Minkah Fitzpatrick is banged up, so this move should help the teams depth.
items.impact: Clark might see a call up if Fitzpatrick misses time, but don't expect the same level of production and expertise.

items.author: Chris Schommer
items.title: Riley Patterson misses field goal in Week 1
items.desc: Riley Patterson converted his lone extra point attempt as well as two of his three field goal attempts to finish with seven points in the Dolphins' 27-13 loss to the Las Vegas Raiders in Week 1.
items.impact: Patterson was unable to remain perfect for head coach Jeff Hafley, missing a field goal attempt late in the third quarter in the loss. The kicker will look to put his miss behind him, with a Week 2 contest against the San Francisco 49ers up next.

items.author: Chris Schommer
items.title: Raiders D/ST disruptive in Week 1 win
items.desc: The Raiders D/ST forced two turnovers (one interception, one fumble recovery) while also registering five sacks in a 27-13 win over the Dolphins in Week 1.
items.impact: The unit took advantage of an underwhelming Miami offense throughout the contest, allowing less than 300 offensive yards in the win. the defense will look for more success against a Los Angeles Chargers offense that could be without wideout Ladd McConkey (chest) in Week 2.

items.author: Chris Schommer
items.title: Matt Gay racks up nine points in Week 1
items.desc: Matt Gay converted both of his field goal attempts as well as all three of his extra point attempts to finish with nine points in the Raiders' 27-13 win over the Miami Dolphins in Week 1.
items.impact: Gay took advantage of his opportunities despite a mixed performance from the Las Vegas offense in the season opener, converting all five of his kick attempts in the win. The kicker will look to remain a stable option moving forward, with a Week 2 contest against the Los Angeles Chargers up next.

items.author: Chris Schommer
items.title: Kirk Cousins offers mixed results in Week 1 win over Dolphins
items.desc: Kirk Cousins completed 21-of-30 pass attempts for 160 yards, three touchdowns, and two interceptions in the Raiders' 27-13 Week 1 win over the Miami Dolphins.
items.impact: Cousins was unable to find much success downfield, averaging just 7.6 yards per completion in the win. the veteran signal-caller will look to minimize turnovers moving forward, with a Week 2 divisional matchup against the Los Angeles Chargers up next.

items.author: Chris Schommer
items.title: Ashton Jeanty leads offense in Week 1 win over Dolphins
items.desc: Ashton Jeanty carried the ball 23 times for 102 yards while also hauling in all six of his targets for a team-leading 45 yards and two touchdowns in the Raiders' 27-13 Week 1 win over the Miami Dolphins.
items.impact: Jeanty was dynamic out of the backfield in the season opener, leading the team in rushing and receiving yards in the win. the running back remains an elite RB1 option with PPR upside for fantasy managers ahead of a Week 2 matchup against the Los Angeles Chargers ahead.

items.author: Chris Schommer
items.title: Mike Washington Jr. sees seven touches in Week 1 win
items.desc: Mike Washington Jr. carried the ball seven times for 41 yards in the Raiders' 27-13 Week 1 win over the Miami Dolphins.
items.impact: Washington Jr. was impactful operating behind Ashton Jeanty in the Las Vegas backfield, averaging 5.9 yards per carry in the win. The running back will look to continue to offer impactful touches as the primary handcuff to Jeanty in the Las Vegas backfield moving forward, with a Week 2 divisional matchup against the Los Angeles Chargers up next.

items.author: Chris Schommer
items.title: Tre Tucker catches two passes in Week 1
items.desc: Tre Tucker caught two of his four targets for 27 yards in the Raiders' 27-13 win over the Miami Dolphins in Week 1.
items.impact: Tucker was one of six to catch at least one pass from Kirk Cousins in the season opener, averaging a team-high 13.5 yards per reception. The wideout remains one of many pass-catching options as part of a revamped Las Vegas offense, with a Week 2 contest against the Los Angeles Chargers up next.

items.author: Garrett Ball
items.title: Da'Shawn Hand (quad) suffers torn quad, likely done for 2026
items.desc: Da'Shawn Hand (quad) suffered a torn quad injury against the Steelers on Sunday that will require surgery. He is likely out for the year but is looking for second opinions.
items.impact: It's another blow to the Falcons who have lost Jalon Walker and James Pearce Jr. already. With Hand out, they'll have to bring in some free agent talent to bolster their ranks.

items.author: Chris Schommer
items.title: Jalen Nailor catches three passes in Week 1
items.desc: Jalen Nailor caught three of his five targets for 27 yards in the Raiders' 27-13 win over the Miami Dolphins in Week 1.
items.impact: Nailor was one of many that saw involvement in the Las Vegas passing offense, finishing as one of six to catch at least one pass in the win. The wideout will look to offer more impactful potential in a revamped Las Vegas offense as the season moves forward, with a Week 2 contest against the Los Angeles Chargers up next.

items.author: Chris Schommer
items.title: Jack Bech finds end zone in Week 1 win
items.desc: Jack Bech caught three of his four targets for 23 yards and one touchdown in the Raiders' 27-13 Week 1 win over the Miami Dolphins.
items.impact: Bech capitalized on modest involvement in the Las Vegas passing attack in the season opener, catching one of the three touchdowns thrown by veteran quarterback Kirk Cousins. The wideout will look for more impactful output as the season continues, with a Week 2 contest against the Los Angeles Chargers up next.

items.author: Chris Schommer
items.title: Michael Mayer hauls in six receptions in Week 1 win
items.desc: Michael Mayer hauled in six of his seven targets for 32 yards in the Raiders' 27-13 Week 1 win over the Miami Dolphins.
items.impact: Mayer took advantage of the absence of No. 1 tight end Brock Bowers, leading the team in targets in the win. The tight end remains a steady option as long as Bowers remains sidelined for fantasy managers, with a Week 2 matchup against the Los Angeles Chargers ahead.

items.author: Chris Schommer
items.title: Malik Benson catches one pass in Week 1
items.desc: Malik Benson caught one of his two targets for six yards in the Raiders' 27-13 win over the Miami Dolphins in Week 1.
items.impact: Benson struggled to make an impact with his minimal target share, finishing sixth on the team in receiving yards. The wideout can be left off rosters in all formats until further notice ahead of a Week 2 contest against the Los Angeles Chargers.

items.author: Chris Schommer
items.title: Cody White sees one target in Week 1
items.desc: Cody White failed to catch his only target in the Raiders' 27-13 win over the Miami Dolphins in Week 1.
items.impact: White was an afterthought in the Las Vegas passing attack, finishing last on the team in targets in the win. The wideout remains best left off rosters in all formats until further notice ahead of a Week 2 contest against the Los Angeles Chargers.

items.author: Chris Schommer
items.title: Malik Willis underwhelms behind center in Week 1 loss to Raiders
items.desc: Malik Willis completed 15-of-27 pass attempts for 220 yards and one interception while also rushing six times for 39 yards and one touchdown in the Dolphins' 27-13 Week 1 loss to the Las Vegas Raiders.
items.impact: Willis struggled to stay upright in the season opener, falling victim to five sacks in the Week 1 loss. The quarterback remains a sneaky option behind center due to his ability to use his feet for positive plays, with a Week 2 matchup against the San Francisco 49ers up next.

items.author: Chris Schommer
items.title: De'Von Achane sees 15 touches in Week 1 loss to Raiders
items.desc: De'Von Achane carried the ball 11 times for 36 yards while also hauling in four of his five targets for 30 yards in the Dolphins' 27-13 Week 1 loss to the Las Vegas Raiders.
items.impact: Achane was unable to find much running room out of the backfield in the season opener, with the Las Vegas defense challenging new starting quarterback Malik Willis to beat it through the air. The running back remains a dynamic option in PPR formats, but fantasy managers may need to temper expectations in the short term, with a Week 2 matchup against the San Francisco 49ers up next.
